result:
The morning began with a small sound, the kettle waking before the birds. I stood at the window, watching light gather along the wet pavement. A bicycle passed, carrying a paper bag and a promise of coffee. Somewhere, a radio played a song that belonged to no one and everyone.

I thought about how we build our days from little pieces, a cup, a key, a step outside. We say ordinary, as if ordinary were the opposite of wonder. But the world insists otherwise. It sends us rain in the face and asks if we will smile every single time.

My mind wandered to a river I had seen once, moving so steadily that it looked like time given a body. I had stood on a bridge and watched the current pull leaves around a stone, remembering that even slow water can carve a canyon. We are like that too.

By noon, I was outside, walking without a plan. The bakery smelled of cinnamon and heat. A child chased a pigeon along the curb, laughing as if the bird had agreed to play. I bought a loaf, broke it in half, and gave a piece to a cat with dignity.

In the afternoon, rain returned. I let it soak my sleeves. I am learning that a life is not made only by grand events, but by these small, repeated choices: to stop, to listen, to share, to let the weather in, and to believe that ordinary grace remains each day.

The morning began with a small sound, the kettle waking before the birds. I stood at the window, watching light gather along the wet pavement. A bicycle passed, carrying a paper bag and a promise of coffee. Somewhere, a radio played a song that belonged to no one and everyone.

I thought about how we build our days from little pieces, a cup, a key, a step outside. We say ordinary, as if ordinary were the opposite of wonder. But the world insists otherwise. It sends us rain in the face and asks if we will smile every single time.

My mind wandered to a river I had seen once, moving so steadily that it looked like time given a body. I had stood on a bridge and watched the current pull leaves around a stone, remembering that even slow water can carve a canyon. We are like that too.
